subject: general
question: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 3 hours and Pipe B in 5 hours. At 7 am, pipe A was opened. At what time will the tank be filled if pipe B was opened at 8 am?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM of 3 and 5 = 15 units.

Efficiency of A = 15 ÷ 3 = 5 units/hr, B = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 units/hr.

A works alone from 7 am to 8 am → Fills 5 units, remaining = 15 − 5 = 10 units.

Both A and B working together take = 10 ÷ (5 + 3) = 10/8 = 1 hour 15 minutes.

Time when the tank is filled = 8:00 am + 1 hour 15 minutes = 9 : 15 am.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 15 am.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 3 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 5 hours

Pipe A was opened at 7 am and Pipe B at 8 am.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (Hours)**
 **Total Capacity (Units)**
 **Efficiency (Units/hr)**
 
 

 A
 3
 15
 5
 
 

 B
 5
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Between 7 am and 8 am (1 hour), only Pipe A is open.

⇒ Water filled by Pipe A in 1 hour = 5 × 1 = 5 units

⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled = 15 − 5 = 10 units

⇒ At 8 am, Pipe B is also opened. Now both are working simultaneously.

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and B = 5 + 3 = 8 units/hour

⇒ Time taken to fill the remaining 10 units = 10 ÷ 8 = 5/4 hours

⇒ 5/4 hours = 1 hour + (1/4 × 60) minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes

⇒ Time at which tank is completely filled = 8:00 am + 1 hour 15 minutes = 9 : 15 am

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 15 am.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Working Formula

If Pipe A fills a tank in 'x' hours and Pipe B fills it in 'y' hours, the time taken when both are opened together is (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours.

Filling and Emptying Pipes

If an inlet pipe fills the tank in 'x' hours and an outlet pipe empties it in 'y' hours, the net filling capacity in 1 hour is (1/x) − (1/y), given x < y.

Time & Work vs Pipes & Cisterns

Both topics follow identical LCM logic. Total work becomes the Total Capacity of the tank, and work done per day becomes the filling rate per hour.
